cards.title: Phrasal Verbs
rule: Definition: Phrasal and Prepositional Verbs (ቅጽል ግሶችን መስተዋድዳዊ ግሶችን) are multi-word verb combinations consisting of a lexical verb paired with an adverbial particle (*phrasal verb*) or a grammatical preposition (*prepositional verb*), resulting in a unified vocabulary unit with a distinct, often highly idiomatic meaning.

Phrasal verbs consist of a main verb and an adverbial particle (e.g., *up, off, out, down, on*). Prepositional verbs, by contrast, consist of a main verb followed strictly by a grammatical preposition (e.g., *look at, cope with, rely on*). The core linguistic challenge is that phrasal verbs are highly idiomatic: their combined meaning is completely different from the literal meanings of the individual words (e.g., *give* [ምሃብ] vs. *give up* [ተስፋ ምቝራጽ/ምሕዳግ]). Since Tigrinya lacks phrasal verbs and relies on single, highly inflected lexical verbs (e.g., "ተስፋ ቆረጸ" for *give up*, "ኣቋረጸ" for *call off*), students must memorize these multi-word combinations as distinct vocabulary items to succeed on national examinations.

Syntactic separability (ስውር ሰዋስው ናይ ምፍልላይ) is a major exam focus for transitive phrasal verbs. If a phrasal verb is separable, a noun object can sit either after the particle or between the verb and the particle ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Particle} + \text{Noun Object}$$ or $$\text{Verb} + \text{Noun Object} + \text{Particle}$$, e.g., "write down the formula" or "write the formula down"). However, if the object is a pronoun (እቲ ተቐባሊ ተውላጠ ስም እንተኾይኑ), it **must** strictly be placed between the verb and the particle ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Pronoun Object} + \text{Particle}$$, e.g., "write *it* down"). Writing $$\times \text{write down it}$$ is a major syntactic error on matriculation exams. Tigrinya speakers often make this error because they naturally want to keep the verbal unit together, reflecting their L1 pronominal suffix habits.

cards.title: Notes
body: Definition: Phrasal and Prepositional Verbs (ቅጽል ግሶችን መስተዋድዳዊ ግሶችን) are multi-word verb combinations consisting of a lexical verb paired with an adverbial particle (*phrasal verb*) or a grammatical preposition (*prepositional verb*), resulting in a unified vocabulary unit with a distinct, often highly idiomatic meaning.

Phrasal verbs consist of a main verb and an adverbial particle (e.g., *up, off, out, down, on*). Prepositional verbs, by contrast, consist of a main verb followed strictly by a grammatical preposition (e.g., *look at, cope with, rely on*). The core linguistic challenge is that phrasal verbs are highly idiomatic: their combined meaning is completely different from the literal meanings of the individual words (e.g., *give* [ምሃብ] vs. *give up* [ተስፋ ምቝራጽ/ምሕዳግ]). Since Tigrinya lacks phrasal verbs and relies on single, highly inflected lexical verbs (e.g., "ተስፋ ቆረጸ" for *give up*, "ኣቋረጸ" for *call off*), students must memorize these multi-word combinations as distinct vocabulary items to succeed on national examinations.

Syntactic separability (ስውር ሰዋስው ናይ ምፍልላይ) is a major exam focus for transitive phrasal verbs. If a phrasal verb is separable, a noun object can sit either after the particle or between the verb and the particle ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Particle} + \text{Noun Object}$$ or $$\text{Verb} + \text{Noun Object} + \text{Particle}$$, e.g., "write down the formula" or "write the formula down"). However, if the object is a pronoun (እቲ ተቐባሊ ተውላጠ ስም እንተኾይኑ), it **must** strictly be placed between the verb and the particle ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Pronoun Object} + \text{Particle}$$, e.g., "write *it* down"). Writing $$\times \text{write down it}$$ is a major syntactic error on matriculation exams. Tigrinya speakers often make this error because they naturally want to keep the verbal unit together, reflecting their L1 pronominal suffix habits.

Inseparable phrasal and prepositional verbs do not allow any separation under any circumstances. Regardless of whether the object is a noun or a pronoun, it must strictly follow the particle or preposition ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Preposition/Particle} + \text{Object}$$, e.g., "look after the children" or "look after *them*"). Writing $$\times \text{look them after}$$ is grammatically incorrect. Common inseparable combinations tested on the ESSLCE include *run into* (to meet by chance), *cope with* (to handle), *rely on* (to trust), and *look after* (to take care of).

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Because of the heavy rainfall and flooding, the school principal had to ________ the sports competition.

steps.text: The context 'heavy rainfall and flooding' indicates that the sports competition had to be canceled.
We need a phrasal verb meaning to cancel.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Because of the heavy rainfall and flooding, the school principal had to ________ the sports competition.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context 'heavy rainfall and flooding' indicates that the sports competition had to be canceled. We need a phrasal verb meaning to cancel.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'put off' (to postpone) with 'call off' (to cancel). While both are common, 'call off' (Option B) is the correct phrasal verb meaning to cancel an event.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Call off' (ምስራዝ) ዝብል ቅጽል ግሲ ንሓደ መደብ ወይ ውድድር ምሉእ ብምሉእ ንምስራዝ የገልግል። 'Put off' (ምስጋጋር) ግን ሓደ መደብ ንኻልእ ግዜ ምስጋጋር ንምግላጽ እዩ። ኣብዚ ብሰንኪ ውሕጅን ከቢድ ዝናብን እቲ ውድድር ስለ ዝተሰረዘ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'call off' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: I have finished reading this reference book; please ________ to the library assistant.

steps.text: 'Hand in' (to submit/return) is a transitive separable phrasal verb.
Since the object is the pronoun 'it', it must strictly be placed between the verb and the particle ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Pronoun} + \text{Particle}$$).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I have finished reading this reference book; please ________ to the library assistant.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Hand in' (to submit/return) is a transitive separable phrasal verb. Since the object is the pronoun 'it', it must strictly be placed between the verb and the particle ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Pronoun} + \text{Particle}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Option B 'hand in it' places the pronoun at the end, which violates the pronoun separation rule. Option D 'hand it down' has an incorrect meaning (to pass to next generation). Option C is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Hand in' (ምምላስ/ምርካብ) ዝብል ቃል ዝፈላለ (separable) ቅጽል ግሲ እዩ። እቲ ተቐባሊ ሓሳብ 'it' (ተውላጠ ስም) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ብግድን ኣብ ማእከል እቲ ግሲን እታ መጣበቕታን ክስራዕ ኣለዎ ('hand it in' - Option C)። 'hand in it' ምጥቃም ዓቢ ናይ ሰዋስው ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: The high school laboratory has ________ chemical solutions, so the practical test has been postponed.

steps.text: The context 'so the practical test has been postponed' indicates that the laboratory has exhausted its supply of chemical solutions.
We need a phrasal verb meaning to exhaust a supply.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The high school laboratory has ________ chemical solutions, so the practical test has been postponed.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context 'so the practical test has been postponed' indicates that the laboratory has exhausted its supply of chemical solutions. We need a phrasal verb meaning to exhaust a supply.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students must identify 'run out of' (Option A) as the correct three-word phrasal verb meaning to exhaust. 'Run into' means to meet by chance, and 'put up with' means to tolerate.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Run out of' (ምውዳእ/ምሕላቕ) ዝብል ሰለስተ ቃላት ዘለዎ ቅጽል ግሲ፡ ዘለካ ቀረብ ወይ ቀዋሚ ነገር ምሉእ ብምሉእ ክውዳእ ከሎ ንምግላጽ የገልግል። ኣብዚ እቲ ኬሚካል ስለ ዝተወድአ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'run out of' (Option A) እዩ።

games.title: Match the phrasal verb to its meaning

questions.q: Because of the heavy rainfall and flooding, the school principal had to ________ the sports competition.
questions.label: 1. Because of the heavy rainfall and flooding, the school princ
why: The context 'heavy rainfall and flooding' indicates that the sports competition had to be canceled. We need a phrasal verb meaning to cancel.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: I have finished reading this reference book; please ________ to the library assistant.
questions.label: 2. I have finished reading this reference book; please ________
why: 'Hand in' (to submit/return) is a transitive separable phrasal verb. Since the object is the pronoun 'it', it must strictly be placed between the verb and the particle ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Pronoun} + \text{Particle}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The high school laboratory has ________ chemical solutions, so the practical test has been postponed.
questions.label: 3. The high school laboratory has ________ chemical solutions,
why: The context 'so the practical test has been postponed' indicates that the laboratory has exhausted its supply of chemical solutions. We need a phrasal verb meaning to exhaust a supply.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: Students must learn how to ________ difficult exam anxiety under intense time pressure.
questions.label: 4. Students must learn how to ________ difficult exam anxiety u
why: 'Cope' is an inseparable prepositional verb that strictly requires the preposition 'with': $$\text{cope with} + \text{Object}$$.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: I cannot ________ his constant complaints during our study sessions anymore.
questions.label: 5. I cannot ________ his constant complaints during our study s
why: The context 'cannot... constant complaints... anymore' indicates that the speaker cannot tolerate his behavior. We need a phrasal verb meaning to tolerate.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The biology question was extremely difficult, but Dawit refused to ________ and kept trying until he solved it.
questions.label: 6. The biology question was extremely difficult, but Dawit refu
why: The context 'refused to [blank] and kept trying' indicates that Dawit did not stop trying. We need a phrasal verb meaning to stop trying or surrender.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The old generator in the school yard ________ yesterday, so we had no electricity during the lab class.
questions.label: 7. The old generator in the school yard ________ yesterday, so
why: 'Break down' (to stop functioning) is an intransitive phrasal verb. Since it has no object, it cannot be passive ($$\times \text{was broken down}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The class representative always ________ the students who are absent from the revision classes.
questions.label: 8. The class representative always ________ the students who ar
why: The context 'students who are absent' indicates that the representative is searching or inquiring about them. We need a prepositional verb meaning to search.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: These old chemical containers are dangerous, so you should ________ immediately.
questions.label: 9. These old chemical containers are dangerous, so you should _
why: 'Throw away' (to discard) is a separable transitive phrasal verb. Since the object is the pronoun 'them', it must strictly be placed in the middle: $$\text{Verb} + \text{Pronoun} + \text{Particle}$$.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The university dean had to ________ her scholarship application because she failed to submit her ESSLCE certificate.
questions.label: 10. The university dean had to ________ her scholarship applicat
why: The context 'because she failed to submit her certificate' indicates that the dean rejected her application. We need a phrasal verb meaning to reject.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q:
A: Is the meeting scheduled for Tuesday? 
B: Yes, but it has been put ___ for Saturday.
why: The phrasal verb 'put off' means to postpone or delay an event to a later time.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: This is a non-smoking area. Could you ________ your cigarette, please?
why: The phrasal verb **'put out'** means to extinguish a fire or a cigarette.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: I am afraid that I will have to __________ the offer
why: To 'turn down' an offer means to reject or refuse it. This fits the context of the sentence.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: The car _____ of gas and I had to phone for help.
why: To 'run out' of something means to have none left. Since the car had no gas, 'ran out' is the correct past tense phrasal verb.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: You will have to _________ me until my mother comes from the university.
why: The phrasal verb 'put up with' means to tolerate or endure someone or something unpleasant.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: My mother doesn't want to retire. She wants to __________ working.
why: The phrasal verb **carry on** means to continue doing something. Since she doesn't want to retire, she wants to continue working.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Jemal: No, I didn’t. I need to __________ the word in the dictionary.
why: The phrasal verb **look up** specifically means to search for information in a reference book like a dictionary or on the internet.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Muktar is going to be late. His car has __________.
why: The phrasal verb 'break down' means a machine or vehicle has stopped working.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: That is the information that I am not prepared to _________.
why: To 'give out' information means to distribute or reveal it to others. The speaker is saying they are not ready to share that information.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Scientists reported that the ozone layer is becoming thinner and thinner because cars and industries are _________ harmful gases.
why: The sentence is in the Present Continuous tense ('are...'). Therefore, the phrasal verb 'give off' (to emit) must be in the -ing form: 'giving off'.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.
